policies.stages: Sample material textures, allow consumer-owned material extensions, resolve the final world normal, then evaluate surface and lighting
policies.flatContract: Renderer consumers use only TA_MaterialConfig, TA_MaterialInputData and TA_MaterialEvaluation; legacy PBR input types remain internal to the interface
policies.evaluationOrder: Build surface, apply anisotropy, evaluate lighting and preserve sampled alpha
policies.extensionBoundary: Procedural masks, layered normals, edge wear and snow may mutate TA_MaterialInputData before TA_EvaluateMaterial
policies.engineBoundary: The interface contains no URP Light, shadow, SH, scene-color or time globals

invariants: All renderer-facing material state crosses three flat structures
Texture sampling is exposed through one TA_SampleMaterial call
Tangent-space normals resolve through one TA_ResolveMaterialNormalWS call
Surface assembly, anisotropy and lighting execute through one TA_EvaluateMaterial call
Legacy PBR input types do not appear in renderer consumers
Both opaque and transparent consumers use the same three-stage interface
Extensions mutate sampled material input before the fixed evaluation order
Sampled alpha is preserved in TA_MaterialEvaluation
Isotropic and anisotropic results remain numerically equal to the established lighting baselines
limitations: Renderer-specific light, shadow, SH and scene-color acquisition remain consumer responsibilities
The interface currently standardizes BaseColor, Normal, ORM and anisotropy; clear coat and subsurface models are not represented
Texture resources remain explicit function arguments because HLSL structures cannot portably own Unity texture objects
Runtime shader compilation and visual inspection require a licensed Unity Editor
